articles.title: SJAA Annual Awards and Board Elections
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomy Association (SJAA) held its annual awards and potluck dinner on February 8, 2020, to recognize members for their significant contributions. Awards were presented to Kaushal Gangakhedkar for his work migrating observer groups, Rob Jaworski for his long-standing service as an officer and in outreach, and Cat Cvengros for single-handedly managing the School Star Party program. Additionally, board elections saw Rob Jaworski, Sandy Mohan, Wolf Witt, and Glenn Newell reelected as Directors.

articles.title: Strategic Meeting Summary
articles.summary: SJAA leaders held a strategic meeting on March 1 to evaluate and determine the organization's future direction for the next few years. The session reaffirmed SJAA's core objective of astronomy education and identified key areas for improvement, particularly concerning internal member engagement, education, and participation in club operations. Further focused meetings and working groups are planned to develop specific action plans for these identified areas.

articles.title: Clear Skies Bring Out the Amateur Astronomers in the Bay Area - SJAA coverage on KCBS Radio Show by Keith Menconi
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) was featured on a KCBS Radio show by Keith Menconi, highlighting the return of amateur astronomers to urban star parties in the Bay Area after a period of winter storms. SJAA President Swami Nigam explained how cloudy weather had led to event cancellations, and the clear skies now allow them to host gatherings, even in parking lots, to educate newcomers and spread the joy of stargazing despite light pollution. The article emphasizes the educational outreach efforts of the SJAA.

articles.title: NASA Selects Four Possible Missions to Study the Secrets of the Solar System
articles.summary: NASA has selected four Discovery Program investigations for concept studies, aiming to deepen our understanding of the solar system's active and complex worlds. These potential missions will focus on Venus (DAVINCI+), Jupiter's moon Io (Io Volcano Observer), and Neptune's moon Triton (Trident), exploring their formation, evolution, and potential for habitability. Each study receives $3 million, with final selections of up to two missions for further development expected next year.

articles.title: NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope Ends Mission of Astronomical Discovery
articles.summary: NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope officially concluded its more than 16-year mission of astronomical discovery in infrared light. As one of NASA's Great Observatories, Spitzer made significant contributions to understanding our solar system, star and planet formation, galaxy evolution, and particularly, the detection and characterization of exoplanets, including the TRAPPIST-1 system. Its impactful legacy will continue to influence future infrared astronomy and pave the way for missions like the James Webb Space Telescope.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article presents a gallery showcasing astrophotography by members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It features multiple deep-sky images, each accompanied by comprehensive technical specifications including the capture date, location, imaging telescope, camera, mount, and software used for acquisition and processing. Notable celestial objects captured include the Cone Nebula, IC443 Supernova, TMB Tadpoles, and Helix Nebula.

articles.title: NSF's newest solar telescope produces first images
articles.summary: The National Science Foundation's Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) has released its first images, showcasing the highest resolution views of the sun's surface ever captured. These images reveal unprecedented details of turbulent "boiling" plasma and intricate magnetic features, offering critical insights into solar convection and the origins of space weather. The telescope is poised to revolutionize solar astronomy, significantly improving our understanding of the sun and our ability to predict potentially disruptive solar storms.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: The 'Kid Spot' article offers space-themed jokes, followed by engaging 'Fun Facts' about the Mars Rover Opportunity and our Sun. It highlights Opportunity's longevity and record-breaking travel, as well as fascinating details about the Sun's energy, size, and recent imaging breakthroughs.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced it is closely monitoring the COVID-19 situation in Santa Clara County, potentially leading to event cancellations, and advises members to check for updates. The article details recent board member re-elections and new appointments, including a new Ephemeris Content Editor and In-Town Star Party coordinator. It also reports on officer elections held in March, where Gerry Joyce became President and Emi Nikolov was elected Secretary, alongside summaries of board discussions on Google Groups migration and strategic planning.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides diverse resources and programs for its members and the community, fostering interest in astronomy across all ages. Offerings include a library, telescope repair services, and regular observing sessions for both solar and night sky phenomena. Additionally, the SJAA supports learning through beginner programs, equipment loaners, astrophotography groups and workshops, and educational outreach via school star parties.
